IIRC, the problem with DOOM 3 was that part of the team left, but some of the big names were still there. Carmack is a genius when it comes to technology and coming up with new ways to do things, I think it's a huge part of why DOOM 3 had such revolutionary graphics at the time. I think Romero was gone by then, and he's good at level design. But it seems like id for their early games were a perfect team. A sort of team where people by themselves weren't able to make a good product, but when they worked together, they all complimented each other perfectly. Even before Bethesda, Quake 4 comes to mind.

I don't think Bethesda makes necessarily bad or overrated games. The reason why they are so polarizing, is because they usually remove and dumb down features in sequels. Some people either don't care they were removed or don't miss those features, but I think a lot of them are upset the game changed so much. My opinion about Bethesda games is that they're not bad, but they're definitely shitting on lifelong fans of the series.
